text:
alex: Heads-up — I found a reproducible window where a prefix gets demoted and immediately rehydrated on another node, but the eviction scorer still treats the old lease as valid. logs: `evict: lease_e=42 != lease_o=41` :confused:
mina: saw a similar spike in canary last week. do you have a tiny repro? :eyes:
alex: yup. simple loop that toggles ownership quickly and reads with prefetch. snippet:
```
# repro loop (pseudocode)
claim_prefix(pfx)
demote_prefix(pfx)
handback_prefix(pfx)
read_with_prefetch(pfx)
```
ryan: what's the expected invariant? strictly monotonic ownership token (epoch + seq) so two nodes can't both believe they're owner? or are we ok with transient overlap?
jessie: current approach uses a soft-lease id only. there's a race: demote completes at owner A, but scorer's metadata still has A's token; handoff to B happens quickly and B serves, but eviction logic relies on matching token and skips reclaim. results in double-serve window.
mina: proposal — upgrade ownership token to a 3-tuple: (epoch, owner_id, commit_seq). eviction requires commit_seq >= seen_seq to accept ownership. that makes decisions deterministic without clock reliance. cost: extra field to carry in handshake/metadata.
ryan: alternative: two-phase demote that returns a grace_cutoff timestamp consumers use to reject older commits. simpler but fragile with clock skew and cross-dc time drift.
alex: leaning toward (epoch,seq). we can piggyback seq in existing handshake and keep perf hit small. also avoids adding clock dependence.
jessie: agree. add an integration test that floods handoffs and asserts no overlapping ownership for >1ms. keep slack-sized assertions.
prefetch-bot: metric alert: prefix_handoff_retries up 8x in canary at 2026-03-17T14:10Z :warning:
mina: action items: (1) I'll draft a short RFC for the (epoch,owner,seq) token + eviction contract, (2) Ryan & Alex implement scorer/handshake changes, (3) Jessie adds canary/replay harness and tests.
ryan: one caveat — upgrades. making seq mandatory means older nodes without seq are treated as seq=0 and could lose ownership post-upgrade. need a compatibility plan: tolerate missing seq by treating null as -inf and require a coordinated rollout or a compatibility flag.
alex: RFC should include transition API: `handshake({owner, epoch, seq || null})` and scorer treats null as -inf until a safe-cutover flag flips. we'll document a staged rollout plan.
mina: timeline? can we do RFC + tests this sprint and a canary next?
jessie: yes. I'll add a `--chaos-fast-handoff` mode to the harness to stress the race and a regression guard.
alex: uploading the repro to the RFC PR. :thumbsup:
mina: great, creating the RFC and tagging owners. keeping the thread for coordination.
ryan: :+1:
jessie: :rocket:
